perf.summary: Hoist the inverse/forward branch out of the innermost loop so the per-butterfly path is branchless.
perf.currentCost: Inside the O(n log n) innermost loop, every butterfly evaluates `if (!inverse)`. Although `inverse` is loop-invariant, it is re-tested n*log n times; the branch also obstructs Burst auto-vectorization of the modular add/sub.
perf.proposedChange: Split each method into two straight-line variants (or branch once on `inverse` before the `len` loop), e.g. an internal FwtOrForward / FwtOrInverse, each containing the triple loop with a single fixed expression `(v+u)%mod` or `(v-u+mod)%mod`. The public RunOr/RunAnd already know the direction at the call site, so dispatch there.
perf.rationale: Removes log n * n/2 branch evaluations and a per-iteration data dependency on a constant, exposing a clean uniform-stride loop body that Burst can SIMD-vectorize (no control flow). Code size grows trivially but I-cache cost is negligible vs. the inner-loop win.
perf.risk: None — identical arithmetic per branch; only the dispatch site moves. Keep `mod` and overflow behavior unchanged.

perf.summary: The `% mod` per butterfly is the dominant cost; it can be replaced by conditional subtraction since operands are already reduced.
perf.currentCost: RunOr/RunAnd/RunXor pre-reduce inputs to [0,mod). A 64-bit hardware integer division (`%`) per butterfly costs ~20-40 cycles and is the single most expensive op in the O(n log n) transform.
perf.proposedChange: For additions where u,v in [0,mod): replace `(u+v)%mod` with `long s=u+v; if(s>=mod) s-=mod;` (or branchless `s -= (mod & -(long)(s>=mod ? 0 : ... ))` form `s -= mod & ((s - mod) >> 63 ^ -1)` — simplest is the conditional-subtract). For subtraction `(u-v+mod)%mod` use `long d=u-v; d += mod & (d>>63);`. The Or-inverse `(v-u+mod)%mod` similarly. Requires u,v already in [0,mod), which the Run* wrappers guarantee, and the transform preserves that invariant (each output is again a single conditional-reduced add/sub).
perf.rationale: Sums of two reduced values are < 2*mod, so at most one subtraction restores range — turning a 20-40 cycle division into a 1-3 cycle add+predicated-subtract. With mod=1e9+7 this is exact; no overflow (2*mod < 2^31).
perf.risk: Only valid because Run* pre-reduces (lines 105-109, etc.) and the butterfly preserves [0,mod). If callers were ever to pass non-reduced data straight into FwtXor (it is private, so they cannot), the invariant could break. The branchless mask form depends on arithmetic right shift of negative longs (well-defined in C#).

perf.summary: Fold the inverse 1/n scaling into the existing pointwise-multiply pass instead of a separate full sweep.
perf.currentCost: RunXor does a pointwise multiply loop (lines 146-149), then FwtXor on c, then a third O(n) loop multiplying by invN (lines 152-155). The final loop is a separate pass over c with its own `* invN % mod`.
perf.proposedChange: The 1/n factor is linear and commutes with the (already-final) state only after the transform, so it cannot fold into the pre-transform multiply. But it CAN be fused: compute invN once, then in the final FwtXor's last layer... simpler and safe: leave as is OR pre-scale by multiplying one operand's pointwise product by invN is invalid. Reject fusing into pre-multiply; instead just confirm the standalone scale loop is minimal. Lower-impact alternative: precompute invN before the transforms so the value is ready (no dependency stall), and mark it const-like.
perf.rationale: Marginal; the scaling must stay post-transform. Listing for completeness — the only real saving is ensuring invN computation (an ExtGcd recursion) is hoisted before the transforms so it overlaps, which it already effectively is.
perf.risk: Do NOT fold invN into the pointwise multiply — that would scale before the inverse transform and change results. Keep the separate post-pass.

perf.summary: ModInverse(n, mod) where n is a power of two and mod is prime can use a closed-form / Fermat path, but ExtGcd recursion is cheap and called once.
perf.currentCost: Recursive ExtGcd is called once per RunXor for invN. Recursion has call overhead and is not Burst-friendly (deep recursion), though depth is ~log mod ≈ 30.
perf.proposedChange: Make ExtGcd iterative (standard loop form with running coefficients) to remove recursion — Burst handles loops far better than recursion and it eliminates stack frames. Single call per RunXor, so impact is small, but recursion is a Burst smell worth removing here and in Fwht.cs.
perf.rationale: Iterative extended-Euclid is the same asymptotics with no call overhead and is Burst-compileable without stack-depth concerns.
perf.risk: Behavior identical if the iterative version returns the same canonical (x,y); ensure the final `(x%mod+mod)%mod` normalization is kept.
